findings.title: Level download/upload to apo-games.de over cleartext HTTP
findings.code_excerpt:
public final static String USERLEVELS_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoMonoMirror4k/get_level.php";
public final static String USERLEVELS_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoMonoMirror4k/save_level.php";
findings.entry_point: App start: ApoMonoPanel.init() (ApoMonoPanel.java:87-90) spawns a thread calling ApoMonoUserlevels.loadUserlevels() -> ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.load() (ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:155); upload path is editor UPLOAD button -> ApoMonoEditor.uploadString() (ApoMonoEditor.java:153) -> ApoMonoUserlevels.addLevel() -> ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.save()
findings.sink: url.openConnection()/getOutputStream()/getInputStream() on the plain-http URLs at ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:122 (save) and :164 (load)
findings.data_path: ApoMonoConstants.USERLEVELS_GETPHP/SAVEPHP -> new URL(...) in ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.load()/save() -> URLConnection with no TLS, no certificate or response validation; response lines are consumed verbatim by input.readLine() (ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:184-209)
findings.attack_scenario: Attacker on the same Wi-Fi (or a DNS hijacker) intercepts the device's connection when the game starts or when a player taps 'upload'. They see every submitted level string and can substitute their own response body for get_level.php, feeding arbitrary 'user levels' (see ApoMonoAndroid-02) into every client. No auth exists on save_level.php either, so they can also poison the shared level database anonymously.
findings.preconditions: Device online (ApoMonoActivity.isOnline(), ApoMonoActivity.java:69-74); attacker positioned for MITM/DNS spoofing of www.apo-games.de. Server availability as of today unknown (domain may be dead), but the client-side behavior is unconditional.
findings.validation_plan: Install the APK on an emulator; redirect www.apo-games.de to a local netcat/mitmproxy listener via /etc/hosts or DNS override. Start the app and observe a cleartext POST 'Get=' to /apoMonoMirror4k/get_level.php; build a level in the editor, press upload, and observe the cleartext POST 'level=...' containing the full level string.

findings.title: Server-controlled level string parsed with substring/charAt and no bounds or error handling
findings.entry_point: HTTP response of get_level.php: each 11th line is stored unvalidated as a level (ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:184-186), copied to ApoMonoLevel.editorLevels (ApoMonoUserlevels.java:30), and selected via menu button 'userlevels' -> ApoMonoMenu.touchedButton (ApoMonoMenu.java:60) -> ApoMonoPanel.setGame (ApoMonoPanel.java:262)
findings.sink: String.substring/charAt/Integer.valueOf in ApoMonoPuzzleGame.loadLevel() (ApoMonoPuzzleGame.java:240-253): expects exactly 3 header digits plus 15*28=420 grid chars; also maps chars >= 'a' via Integer.valueOf(c)-87 with no range check
findings.data_path: readLine() in ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.load() -> levels ArrayList -> getAllLevelsSorted() (ApoMonoUserlevels.java:44-57) -> ApoMonoLevel.editorLevels -> loadLevel(p[0], true, null) picks l = ApoMonoLevel.editorLevels[p[0]] (ApoMonoPuzzleGame.java:230) -> direct parsing with no try/catch on the touchedButton call chain
findings.attack_scenario: MITM (or anyone able to poison the level DB anonymously, see finding 01) answers get_level.php with a line like 'ab' or a 100-char string. Victim taps the 'userlevels' menu button; loadLevel throws NumberFormatException ('a') or StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (short string) on the UI/engine thread, crashing the app every time the button is pressed. Non-digit header chars or oversized unicode grid chars additionally inject out-of-range tile ids into level[][] (memory-safe in Java, but corrupts game logic).
findings.preconditions: Attacker controls the HTTP response (MITM/hijacked DNS/dead-domain takeover) or the server DB; victim must be online and tap the userlevels button. ApoMonoUserlevels.sortByUpload requires s.length() > 2 (ApoMonoUserlevels.java:63), so a 3+ char malformed string passes the only filter that exists.
findings.validation_plan: Two-step: (1) Unit-level - call new ApoMonoPuzzleGame(panel).loadLevel(0,true,"ab") and observe NumberFormatException, or loadLevel(0,true,"000"+'1'.repeat(50)) and observe StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at charAt. (2) End-to-end - MITM get_level.php to return one short line, install APK on emulator with overridden DNS, start app (auto-load), tap 'userlevels', capture the uncaught exception and crash in logcat.

findings.title: SharedPreferences progress string split and used as array index without bounds check
findings.entry_point: The local SharedPreferences file ApoMonoPref (name from ApoMonoConstants.PREFS_NAME, ApoMonoConstants.java:17), read at every startup in ApoMonoPanel.loadPreferences (ApoMonoPanel.java:134-135): settings.getString("solvedLevels", "")
findings.sink: this.solvedLevels[value] = true in ApoMonoSave.createArrayFromString (ApoMonoSave.java:33) against boolean[10000] allocated at ApoMonoSave.java:10; Integer.valueOf(array[i]) at line 32
findings.data_path: /data/data/.../shared_prefs/ApoMonoPref.xml -> getString("solvedLevels") -> createArrayFromString -> split(",") -> Integer.valueOf -> unchecked index into solvedLevels[10000]; the same value later drives level unlocking via getMaxCanChoosen() = solvedCout + 2 (ApoMonoPanel.java:395-401)
findings.attack_scenario: (a) Cheat: a rooted user (or anyone restoring an adb backup/app-altered XML) sets solvedLevels to '0,1,2,3,...' and instantly unlocks all built-in levels; progress is never re-verified. (b) Crash-on-boot: setting a token >= 10000 (e.g. '99999') throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException inside init(), and a non-numeric token throws NumberFormatException, both making the app crash at startup until the pref file is cleared. No untrusted remote input reaches this sink; it is purely local tampering, hence theoretical for remote attackers.
findings.preconditions: Root access, adb backup/restore of another app's prefs, or any local modification of ApoMonoPref.xml. Not reachable through network or level data.
findings.validation_plan: On a rooted emulator: run 'am force-stop net.apogames.apomono', edit /data/data/net.apogames.apomono/shared_prefs/ApoMonoPref.xml to <string name="solvedLevels">99999</string>, relaunch, and observe ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in logcat at ApoMonoSave.createArrayFromString followed by a startup crash loop; replace with '0,1,2' to confirm all early levels become selectable.

categories_checked_and_absent: remote_code_loading - no ClassLoader/defineClass/DexClassLoader/URLClassLoader anywhere in the tree (grep over all 106 .java files returned none)
untrusted_deserialization - no ObjectInputStream, Serializable, or Parcelable misuse; grep found zero matches
weak_integrity_check - no MessageDigest/MD5/hash or signature verification exists at all; downloads are consumed with no integrity layer whatsoever

unsafe_native_call - System.loadLibrary appears only in vendored third-party _from_jar_andmodplug*/PlayerThread.java:912; the game's own audio (ApoMonoMusicPlayer.java:56) uses android MediaPlayer with packaged R.raw resources and no native code path is exercised by game code

path_traversal - game source performs no filesystem I/O at all: no FileInputStream/File/openFileInput/getExternalStorage/user.home constructs outside the vendored midi lib; saves go exclusively to SharedPreferences
credential_or_secret_exposure - only hardcoded value is the public AdMob publisher id 'a1510eb01a099dc' (ApoMonoActivity.java:80), which ships in every APK by design; no API keys or passwords
legacy_sandbox_assumption - no applet/JNLP/desktop entry points; pure Android activity (ApoMonoActivity extends BitsApp)
information_disclosure - uploads contain only the encoded level string (ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:133); no device identifiers or personal data transmitted by game code

resource_exhaustion - all parse buffers are fixed-size arrays (int[15][30], boolean[10000]); the readLine loop in ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.load() could accumulate unbounded list entries from a hostile server, but that reduces to the already-reported hostile-server scenario and causes only heap growth
notes: This Android variant is much smaller in attack surface than the desktop corpus siblings: the entire untrusted-input surface is the two PHP endpoints and the local SharedPreferences blob. There is no AndroidManifest.xml in this dump (source-tree only, with a mirrored nested path 'Users/eliahilse/...' inside the repo), so INTERNET permission and cleartext config could not be verified directly, but the http:// usage implies android.permission.INTERNET in the shipped APK. The vendored '_from_jar_android-midi-libv3*' and '_from_jar_andmodplug*' trees are third-party libraries (com.leff.midi, com.peculiargames.andmodplug); the game code references neither directly (music via MediaPlayer raw resources), so their internals were not treated as reachable. ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad uses deprecated DataInputStream.readLine(). NumberFormatException from Float/Integer.valueOf inside load() (ApoMonoUserlevelsLoad.java:188-206) IS caught by the broad catch(Exception) in ApoMonoUserlevels.loadUserlevels() (lines 23-37), so only the level-string parse in ApoMonoPuzzleGame.loadLevel - which sits outside any handler - crashes the app. Findings 01-03 are flagged shared_component because the net.apogames.<game>.userlevels.{Save,Userlevels,UserlevelsLoad} trio, the apo-games.de/php endpoint constants, and the hand-rolled level-string parser are structural clones expected to recur across the ~26 corpus variants with per-game renames.
